claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Intrinsic lattice distortion governs the enhanced plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion stabilizes a nanostructured microstructure in WTaTiVZr.
The stabilized WTaTiVZr nanostructure contains fine, distributed nanoprecipitates.
The stabilized WTaTiVZr nanostructure contains high-angle grain boundaries.
Nanoprecipitates and high-angle grain boundaries facilitate dislocation nucleation, motion, and dynamic recovery.
The WTaTiVZr nanostructure reduces dislocation pile-up.
The WTaTiVZr nanostructure retards crack propagation.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and retarded crack propagation improve plastic strain and toughness.
Brittle intergranular fracture typically limits pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten lacks the nanostructural mitigating features attributed to WTaTiVZr.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater elongation before fracture than identically processed pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness and greater energy absorption than identically processed pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to remain valid at controlled strain rates up to approximately 1600 degrees Celsius.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten with comparable grain sizes and under identical high-temperature conditions is the proposed controlled comparison.
TEM and high-resolution EBSD can be used to compare nanoprecipitate distributions, grain-boundary angles, and dislocation-related microstructural evolution in the two materials.
